decisions.summary: Quote detection covers plain-text quotes, not just blockquotes - FINDING-4.4
decisions.rationale: Cycle 4 enforced links per '>' block. The prompt asks for markdown and for a verbatim quote with its link, but never for blockquote syntax; the model frequently writes 'Strongest quote: "..." https://...'. With no blockquotes present the per-quote rule found nothing and fell through to the aggregate check FINDING-3.5 was raised about. I validated a format the producer never promised.
decisions.tradeoff: Needs a heuristic for what a quote is. Keyed on a quotation-marked span, which is what the model actually produces.
decisions.test_implication: Plain-text quotes with and without links; ensure _quote_blocks keeps its blockquote-only meaning.

decisions.summary: Two further holes found by hand, not by the suite
decisions.rationale: (a) the quoted-span regex required 2+ inner characters, so 'A' was invisible and short quotes produced zero units. (b) MORE SERIOUS: the trailing-attribution rule absorbed the next non-blank line into a blockquote, so a linked blockquote followed by an unlinked plain-text quote swallowed the latter and the digest was ACCEPTED - a live INV-10 violation that passed every test in the suite. The trailing line is now only absorbed when it is not itself a quote.
decisions.tradeoff: An attribution line that happens to contain quotation marks is now treated as its own quote and must carry a URL.
decisions.test_implication: HIGHEST VALUE REGRESSION THIS CYCLE: linked blockquote immediately followed by an unlinked plain-text quote must be rejected. Also single-character quoted spans and smart quotes.

decisions.summary: Opt-in migration reconciles a wrong or invalid existing index - FINDING-4.5
decisions.rationale: IF NOT EXISTS matches on the index NAME only, so an invalid leftover from a failed concurrent build, or an index on the wrong operator class, is accepted and Alembic then records 0002. specs/04 warns the wrong opclass silently gives worse neighbours rather than erroring; this made that silent failure reachable through the documented procedure and stamped as done.
decisions.tradeoff: The migration now drops an index it did not create. Safe because both names are owned by this migration. Offline --sql mode skips reconciliation, which needs a connection.
decisions.test_implication: The INVALID-index half is untested (Codex reproduced wrong-opclass only); build one by cancelling a concurrent build. Also assert offline --sql still emits both statements.

decisions.summary: Opt-in tolerance applies to `upgrade` only - FINDING-4.6
decisions.rationale: DECISION-4.1 made EVERY alembic command a no-op on an opt-in database: `downgrade base` exited 0, printed nothing, and left all five tables and revision 0002 intact. A command reporting success for work it did not do is worse than the error it suppressed - the error is survivable, the false success is what you act on.
decisions.tradeoff: Depends on Alembic naming its per-command migration function (`upgrade`/`downgrade`/`do_stamp`). First attempt read context.context_opts in env.py, which does not exist there because alembic.context is a module of proxy FUNCTIONS, not the EnvironmentContext - it silently read {} and disabled the tolerance entirely. The check now runs after context.configure(), which copies those options onto the MigrationContext.
decisions.test_implication: `stamp` and `history` on an opt-in database must also not report false success - only `downgrade` was reproduced.

test_targets: HIGHEST VALUE: a linked blockquote immediately followed by an unlinked plain-text quote must be rejected - this violated INV-10 while passing every existing test
Single-character quoted spans ("A") are detected as quotes at all
Smart quotes are treated as quotes
A quote whose URL is a markdown link [text](https://...) - unverified shape, _URL_RE should match inside it but nothing asserts that
alembic stamp and alembic history on an opt-in database must not report false success (only downgrade was reproduced)
The reconcile path for an INVALID index specifically - the wrong-opclass half is covered, the invalid half shares the mechanism but is untested
Offline `alembic -c alembic.deferred.ini upgrade head --sql` still emits both CREATE statements without inspecting a connection
known_edge_cases: FULL SUITE: 112 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, against PostgreSQL 16.13 + pgvector 0.8.5 on port 55440.

Hand-verified: planting a vector_l2_ops index then opting in reconciles it to vector_cosine_ops and valid; default `downgrade base` after opt-in exits 255 with the schema intact; default `upgrade head` after opt-in still exits 0.

PATTERN WORTH NOTING: all three cycle-4 findings, and both extra holes found this cycle, were cases where a fix was correct for the shape it was tested against and wrong just outside it. Two of them produced SILENT NO-OPS rather than errors.
_quote_units treats any quotation-marked line as a quote needing a URL. An attribution line containing quotation marks will now be required to carry one.

findings.detail: A fresh upgrade creates all five tables; a later default upgrade after opt-in exits successfully; revisions in neither chain still fail loudly.
A live concurrent HNSW build permits a second pipeline write while an earlier write transaction remains open.
Documented blockquote shapes work, and ten blockquotes with nine links are rejected while naming the offender.
Two plain-text Strongest quote entries with one aggregate URL are accepted because per-quote enforcement only recognizes Markdown blockquotes.
IF NOT EXISTS accepts an existing wrong-opclass or invalid HNSW index and Alembic still records revision 0002.
After opt-in, default alembic downgrade base exits 0 without changing the revision or removing any schema because the early return is not scoped to upgrade.

findings.target: manual LLM and digest acceptance criteria
findings.detail: Pain-point normalization, vertical disagreements, and digest usefulness still require human review of actual model output.

open_blockers.detail: Manual LLM and digest quality criteria have no assertion form: pain-point normalization, vertical disagreements, and digest usefulness need a human reading real model output. The pipeline has still never run against real data, so these cannot be exercised yet.
